공통: One continuous shot, no cuts. The camera is locked off exactly as in the start frame: no zoom, no pan, no tilt, no shake. Keep the exact handmade needle-felt miniature look of the start frame in every frame: fine wool felt fibres, visible stitches, matte felt and wool; every object keeps its shape, size and colour and never turns into a realistic thing. MONGLE is the coral-pink felt blob. At rest its face is only its two glossy black bead eyes: no nose and no mouth. When its feeling changes, its whole face changes to show that feeling, as written in ACTION, always in needle-felt: the eyes may grow bigger and rounder, squeeze shut into short curved dark stitched lines, curve into happy arcs or droop under little felt lids; a small simple felt mouth may open, smile, pout or wobble; blush, a felt sweat drop or a felt teardrop may appear. When the feeling passes, the mouth and the drops go away and the face returns to rest. Open eyes always stay glossy black beads: no white sclera, no coloured iris, no sparkling cartoon eyes, no eyelashes, no human teeth or lips. Mongle has NO arms, NO legs, NO hands and NO neck, ever: no limbs ever grow, nothing ever sticks out of its body. It moves only by tilting, squashing, stretching and bouncing its whole soft dome body. LOOK: the same light and colours as the start frame, unchanged to the last frame. Apart from Mongle's own expression, nothing new appears that is not in the start frame. If MONGLE is not in the start frame it never comes in. MONGLE does not blink. No speed lines, no motion lines, no cartoon effects, no steam, no smoke. No text, no letters, no numbers, no logos. No sound.

클립.prompt: Wide shot of the winter-night hotteok cart from the start frame. ACTION: from 0 to 0.8 s Grandma takes one small step toward the counter, smiling politely, hands together; from 1.0 to 2.2 s Mongle leans its whole dome forward and nudges the single paper cup across the counter toward Grandma, its face at rest with round bead eyes; from 2.4 s to the end Grandma looks down at the cup. The friend keeps turning a hotteok on the griddle with his spatula the whole time. Grandma is the felt grandmother with short tight curly silver-grey perm hair, a burgundy flower-quilted vest over a cream turtleneck and a long open plum-purple padded coat, no glasses: her face, hair and clothes stay exactly the same in every frame. The friend is the young felt man with short straight black wool hair with soft bangs, a heather-grey felt hoodie and a mustard felt apron: his face, hair and clothes stay exactly the same in every frame. The hotteok stay inside their plain white paper cups; no cup falls, nothing flies through the air. No steam, no smoke rises from the griddle. Mongle never grows arms or legs and never stands up or hops: the scalloped bottom edge of its felt hem stays resting on the surface the whole time, with nothing ever showing under it; it moves cups only by nudging them with its whole soft dome body. Nothing is drawn over the picture.
